chunks: And in another saying of his (peace be upon him), this runs in the same manner:
ai.seo_question: What does 'yajri hadha al-majra' mean in the context of Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This transitional phrase, 'wa fi kalamin akhari lahu' (and in another of his sayings), serves as a rhetorical bridge in Nahj al-Balagha, linking the current narration to the preceding discourse on the hierarchical nature of *Amr bil Ma'ruf wa Nahi anil Munkar* (commanding right and forbidding wrong). It underscores the scholarly view that Imam Ali’s teachings on social reform are not isolated incidents but part of a cohesive, multi-layered framework for civic responsibility. This connection highlights the continuity of his guidance on how believers should escalate their response to evil, from personal conviction to public action.
